universities.name: Carol Davila University of Medicine and Pharmacy
universities.summary: Carol Davila University of Medicine and Pharmacy in Bucharest, tracing back to the 1857 National School of Medicine and Pharmacy, runs a direct-entry, six-year English-medium General Medicine programme leading to the Doctor Medic degree. The university is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG-certification eligibility, and its Romanian medical qualification carries automatic recognition across the EU/EEA under Directive 2005/36/EC Annex V.
universities.campusLifestyle: International students in the English-medium General Medicine programme are based on the university's main Dionisie Lupu Street campus in central Bucharest, with a dedicated International Students Office supporting the admissions and enrollment process.
universities.cityProfile: Bucharest is Romania's capital and largest city, with an international airport, a large resident student population and an established international-student community built up over decades at the country's oldest and largest medical university.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year, 360-ECTS General Medicine programme combines preclinical foundation sciences with clinical training across multiple affiliated hospitals in Bucharest, culminating in the Doctor Medic degree, a Romanian medical qualification with automatic EU/EEA recognition under Directive 2005/36/EC and ECFMG-certification eligibility for US-pathway graduates.
universities.hostelOverview: The university's own accommodation page states that off-campus rent in Bucharest can be as low as EUR 150 per month, not including utilities, and that self-funded international students may apply for dormitory rooms (blocks U1-U6) subject to availability alongside state-scholarship students housed separately. No specific current dormitory fee amount is published for self-funded international students.
universities.dietarySupport: Campus and nearby student cafeterias serve the university community; no separate university-run meal-plan cost is published.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found during research. Admissions and student queries for international applicants are handled through the International Students Office.
universities.studentSupport: International applicants apply through the university's dedicated exam/admissions platform and are supported by the International Students Office at the university's Nicolae Filipescu Street address in Bucharest.

faq.question: Is the English General Medicine programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. Admission requires completion of an accredited high school whose diploma grants access to university studies in the applicant's home country; no prior university degree is required.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the Doctor Medic degree, a Romanian medical qualification listed under EU Directive 2005/36/EC Annex V for automatic recognition across the EU/EEA, and eligible for ECFMG Certification for graduation years 1953-current.

faq.question: Is there a written entrance exam?
faq.answer: No. Admission follows an online registration, a 15-30 minute English-language interview based on published scientific topics, and a ranking that combines the interview score with an Evaluation Grid based on prior school performance.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: EUR 10,000 per year for non-EU international students (EU/EEA citizens pay the RON equivalent at the National Bank of Romania exchange rate), confirmed current for the 2026/27 academic year by Board approval (11 May 2026) and Senate approval (13 May 2026).

faq.question: Are there other admission fees besides tuition?
faq.answer: Yes. Official documents list a EUR 500 language test fee and a 2,500 LEI general registration fee, plus a 200 LEI enrollment fee; it was not confirmed whether the language test fee and registration fee are the same charge or two separate ones.

faq.question: What English-proficiency proof is required?
faq.answer: A minimum B2 CEFR-level English certificate not older than 2 years, unless the applicant completed secondary schooling in English or achieved B2-equivalent English in their baccalaureate exam.

faq.question: When is the next intake and application deadline?
faq.answer: The academic year starts in September. For 2026/27 the university ran two admission sessions: Session I registration closed 13 July 2026 with the ranking published 21 July 2026, and Session II registration was extended to 10 September 2026 for EU citizens and non-EU applicants who already hold a valid visa for Romania, with online interviews to 15 September 2026, ranking on 16 September 2026 and General Medicine file submission on 28-30 September 2026.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available?
faq.answer: Self-funded international students may apply for dormitory rooms subject to availability, though no current fee is published; off-campus rent in Bucharest can be as low as EUR 150 per month, excluding utilities.

faq.question: Can this degree be used to practice medicine outside Romania?
faq.answer: The Doctor Medic qualification carries automatic recognition across the EU/EEA under Directive 2005/36/EC, and graduates are eligible for ECFMG Certification for the US pathway. For India specifically, graduates would need to separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission screening requirements; this was not independently verified against an NMC source during research.

fee.notes: Officially published 2026/27 tuition: EUR 10,000/year for non-EU international students, approved by the university's Board of Directors (11 May 2026) and Senate (13 May 2026) and confirmed on the live admissions page. EU/EEA citizens pay the RON equivalent at the National Bank of Romania exchange rate on the day of payment. Total is calculated as the annual figure times 6 years -- not published as a lump sum. A separate EUR 500 language test fee and a 2,500 LEI registration fee also apply; it was not confirmed whether these are the same charge in two currencies or two distinct fees.
